hypothesis-r6-rbe.statement: dev-infra's pull_request CI (pr.yml) runs fork-PR code (merge commit: BUILD files, .bazelrc.common, bazel/remote-execution/BUILD.bazel all attacker-editable via local_path_override @devinfra) under --config=remote against Google-internal RBE instance internal-200822/primary_instance using the embedded GCP SA credential; the DEFAULT platform is platform_with_network (dockerNetwork=standard) and the attacker can redefine exec_properties (network mode incl. google_private, Pool, container-image) in their PR. Confirmed statically: untrusted code executes on internal build infrastructure; escalation hypothesis (internal-network reach) unverified.

hypothesis-r8-preview-race.impact_ceiling: attacker content on Angular preview infra channel + arbitrary-issue bot comments; no secrets/code-exec in deploy job
hypothesis-r8-preview-race.statement: The preview pack action (pack-and-upload-artifact) runs in the SAME job as the fork-controlled bazel build (consumer wiring verified: angular/angular adev-preview-build.yml build+pack same job); a fork daemon spawned during the build continuously overwrites the deterministic metadata path ($RUNNER_TEMP/pack-and-upload-tmp-dir/__metadata__pull_number.txt) between the inject and tar steps, so the uploaded artifact carries attacker-chosen pull-number/revision. The trusted workflow_run deploy job (pull-requests:write + FIREBASE_PREVIEW_SERVICE_TOKEN) then extracts these values with ZERO validation (extract-artifact-metadata.ts reads+trims) and uses them as channelId (action.yml:103) and sticky-comment number (action.yml:112): attacker content can overwrite another PR's preview channel and the bot comments on arbitrary issues.
hypothesis-r8-preview-race.suspected_invariant: artifact-derived metadata is trusted by the deploy job without validation or integrity binding
hypothesis-r8-preview-race.trust_boundary: fork build job -> artifact -> trusted workflow_run deploy job
